tip_title: Fall Is When Most People Renew. It's Also When Most People Miss This.
topic: Home Insurance - Open Enrollment / Annual Review Trigger
blurb:
💡 **Insurance Tip: Fall Is When Most People Renew. It's Also When Most People Miss This.**

A lot of homeowners policies renew in the fall, and most people just let them roll over without a second look. That's fine — until you realize the remodel you did in the spring, the new appliances you bought, or the fence you put in over the summer aren't reflected in your coverage. Your insurer doesn't automatically know your house got better. You have to tell them.

This doesn't have to be a big project. Pull up your declarations page and ask one question: does the dwelling coverage number still match what it would actually cost to rebuild your home today? Construction costs have moved a lot over the last few years, and a number set two or three years ago may be running behind. Same goes for personal property — if you've added anything significant, your contents limit should reflect it.

Not sure where to start? Your Peachy agent can walk through your current coverage and flag anything that's drifted out of date — usually takes one quick conversation.

📖 [Learn more from the NAIC](https://content.naic.org/article/consumer-insight-searching-homeowners-insurance-policy-tips-get-most-value)
summary: Covers the homeowners policy annual renewal as a prompt to update dwelling and personal property limits after home improvements or new purchases made during the year, framed as a fall renewal timing action item rather than a post-renovation trigger or general annual review habit.
scoring_notes: Both newsletters have strong homeowner populations (78% East Cobb, 55% Perimeter, 65% Lewisville Lake). Fall is a natural renewal season and a real behavioral moment. Prior tips on annual review (July 20) and renovation-trigger review (April 27) were framed around post-project prompts and broad renewal habits — this tip angles specifically on the fall renewal calendar as the moment AND the summer-project accumulation (remodel, appliances, fence) as the concrete reason to act now. Differentiated angle: seasonal timing + accumulated mid-year changes as a combined prompt, neither of which was the prior tip's frame. Source is NAIC, fully trusted.
